instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Line two baking sheets with parchment.

Trim the zucchini and slice them lengthwise into slabs about 1/4 inch thick. Spread them in a single layer on the two sheets. Drizzle with 2 tbsp of the oil, sprinkle with 1/2 tsp of the salt, and roast for 12 to 14 minutes, until soft and lightly golden at the edges. No need to turn them.
Meanwhile, finely dice the onion. Warm the remaining 1 tbsp oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 3 minutes, until soft.
Add the passata, 8 of the basil leaves torn up, the rest of the salt and the pepper. Simmer for 10 minutes. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
While the sauce simmers, slice the mozzarella thin and pat the slices dry with paper towels. Grate the Parmesan. That should be about 1 cup.
Spread 1/2 cup of the sauce over the bottom of a 9 by 13 inch baking dish. Lay half the zucchini on top, then 1 cup of sauce, half the mozzarella and 1/3 cup of the Parmesan.
Add the rest of the zucchini, the rest of the sauce, the rest of the mozzarella and the rest of the Parmesan.
Bake for 12 minutes, until the cheese is melted and the edges are bubbling. Let it rest for 5 minutes.
Tear the remaining basil over the top. Cut into squares and serve.
method_notes: The sources agree on the no-breading method: roast sliced zucchini until soft, then layer with tomato sauce, mozzarella and Parmesan and bake. They differ on slice thickness and bake time. This version roasts at 425°F and bakes briefly because every layer is already hot and cooked, which keeps it inside 50 minutes. None of the pages had ratings, so the lead is the version closest to the dish's name and method.
